title: Judge scheduling: capacity-fill (not idle-fill) + parallel fan-out, budget-capped
summary: Refines the idle-fill heartbeat wiring (#6). Pure idle-fill is too timid for an orchestrator. Correct model = CAPACITY-FILL: headroom = maxConcurrency − running(in_progress tasks). Each heartbeat spawns ready tasks into the headroom FIRST (tasks always win), then fans out PARALLEL edge-judge efforts into the leftover slots. Knobs (loop config, configurable): maxConcurrency=10, judge fan-out caps at 6 parallel efforts/heartbeat (chosen over 'all spare slots' to avoid token spikes / momentary task starvation, and over conservative 2-3 for faster backlog drain). decideAll must be able to return BOTH spawn tasks AND a judge directive {parallel:K, budget:N} in one heartbeat. Parallelism is safe: daemon is single-threaded Node so K concurrent /judge/next calls return DISJOINT cursor slices (no double-judge); token budget still caps TOTAL spend (parallel = faster drain, not more spend). Mostly matters for the one-time ~263-edge backlog (sequential ~44 ticks at budget 6 vs ~7 ticks at 6-wide). Busy orchestrator (running near cap) → judging auto-backs-off; quiet → drains hard. Grounded in existing decideAll: 'running' (in_progress count, daemon.js:476) and shared per-heartbeat 'batch' pool already exist. MUST be built AFTER #6 (same decideAll function — sequential to avoid the daemon.js clobber race).
